entries.name: first-touch-1-what-it-is

body.rule: What it is. First-touch text is what a cold reader sees before deciding to keep going: the email subject and preview, every Reel cover and on-screen hook, the first b-roll screen and carousel slide 1. The five rules below apply to every one of them (R59).

entries.reason: Plan section 4.3, first-touch rules (R59), stated in general terms

body.rule: Specific. It names the concrete subject (ads, Google, Meta, the budget, inquiries, bookings, the landing page), so a cold reader knows what it is about without the rest of the piece. A line lifted from a client or a call keeps its subject: a question about "this" or "it" says what "this" is.

Slide 1 carries the promise. The carousel's title, or its promise as an insight about the reader, is on slide 1. A bare quote, a teaser or a slide that only makes sense after slide 2 is not a slide 1.

Subject lines state WIA's counter-expected point or decision, or the reader's own question or problem, in plain first-person or observational words. Never a narration of what a third party did (a client, a platform, an AI tool). Two to four options, best first; the preview text finishes the thought, it does not repeat it.

No insider terms. WIA's program internals (the insider terms in document 05: office hours, the VAULT, VIP Day, the kickoff call and the rest) never appear in first-touch text; in a script, an email or a caption each appears at most once, explained in plain words ("we met with one of our Accelerator members recently"). Offer names are not insider terms: they carry their approved descriptors (document 05).

entries.name: first-touch-6-who-did-what

body.rule: Who did what. A story beat keeps the actor the record names (the client, her own tool or assistant, WIA's strategist), or the fact Whitney attested at a gate. Specificity outranks sibling distinctness: when two openings in a pack or a week would collide, the later one changes its angle and keeps its subject.

entries.reason: Plan section 4.3, first-touch rule 5 and the closing rule on specificity

entries.name: first-touch-7-her-subject-lines

body.rule: Her own subject lines, sent 2026 (patterns, not formulas; never reuse one): "More leads won't fix this..."; "The goal isn't going viral"; "Visibility isn't something you earn." (preview: "You engineer it."); "The question we ask every new client" (preview: "I'm always surprised by the answer"); "It feels like our sales are on autopilot."; "She didn't post on Instagram for 10 weeks"; "What I taught my clients this week"; "If your ads aren't performing like they should, read this". A quote, an observation or a plain first-person statement, mostly without emoji, never a "What happens next?" tease.
